title: Telemetry hourglass lane and deployment brief (June 2027) - doodle
content:
Quick sketch / purpose:
This is an informal deployment brief for the feature bundle we’re shipping in mid-June. The document focuses on the telemetry cadence (hourglass-style), operator rotations, and a compact set of check actions for preflight, canary progression, and the 72h aftercare window.

High level intent:
- Keep the first 8 hours tightly instrumented with minute-level samples for key signals.
- Use a small cohort canary (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) with quiet windows between steps.
- Ensure fallback routes and model-variant circuits are primed for instant flip.
- Collect example prompts and a small prompt-suite for automatic quality checks at each gate.

Owners and roles (tentative):
- Release lead: Ava Chen (primary comms, go/no-go)
- Observability lead: Marcus Patel (dashboards, signal owners)
- SRE on-call: Sofia Rivera (pager escalation)
- Rollback gate & ops: Liam O'Connor (rollback choreography + runbook owner)
- QA/test harness: Nina Gomez (smoke tests, regression checks)

Channels:
- Slack: #deploy-telemetry-hourglass (primary)
- Incident bridge: zoom.us/room/telemetry-launch (warm standby 15m before go)
- Pager channel: PagerDuty INF-SRE

Preflight checklist (T-72h -> T-0):
- T-72h: Finalize smoke test matrix and ensure updated fixtures (Nina).
- T-48h: Load-test plan for canary path validated at expected QPS (Marcus).
- T-24h: Verify KMS keys / secrets for private deploy paths (Security).
- T-6h: Dry run of smoke tests against staging with production-scale traces enabled.
- T-2h: Bake small sampling config: 1m granularity for latency buckets, 10s granularity for request failures, full traces for 1% of requests.
- T-30m: Confirm roll-forward and rollback playbook accessible in runbook repo.
- T-10m: Final preflight signoff from Release lead and Observability lead.

Canary progression (recommended increments):
- Step 0 (baseline): 0% production traffic, run through smoke + example prompts.
- Step 1: 1% traffic -> 30m quiet window; evaluate service-level signals.
- Step 2: 5% traffic -> 60m quiet window; validate quality checks and tail latency.
- Step 3: 20% traffic -> 90m quiet window; check cost anomalies and KV cache hit ratio.
- Step 4: 100% traffic -> monitoring ramp 4h, final signoff after 8h of stable signals.

Hourglass telemetry cadence (what to sample when):
- First hour after each progression event: 10s sampling for error counts and 1s for 95/99 latency percentiles on the canary subset.
- Hours 1–8: 1m sampling for all primary metrics; keep traces for 5% requests for the canary cohort.
- Hours 8–24: 5m sampling; reduce traces to 1% but keep prefix/KV cache telemetry active.
- 24–72 hours: 15m sampling; focus on slowly moving signals (memory growth, GC pause trends, infra errors).

Key signals and thresholds (quick reference):
- End-to-end p50/p95/p99 latency (user-experienced): p95 increase > 30% from baseline => hold progression.
- Request failure rate: > 0.5% absolute increase or 3x relative increase => immediate investigation, hold.
- Model correctness smoke test (prompt-suite): > 5% regression in golden prompt set => rollback candidate.
- KV cache hit ratio: drop > 10 percentage points relative to baseline => investigate degraded cache priming.
- CPU/GPU utilization: sustained > 85% on serving nodes => prepare capacity expansion or throttle route.
- Outbound cost anomaly: > 20% spike in token cost per minute => pause and inspect routing rules.

Quick smoke test matrix (executed at each gate):
- Sanity: basic generation end-to-end, check content tokens, and timing.
- Consistency: run 50 golden prompts; expect at most 3 mismatches.
- Load-sensitive: run 100 concurrent short-sequence requests to canary to validate batching behaviour.
- Edge-cases: truncated prompts, null input, tool-calling flow (if enabled).

Immediate remediation steps (if a gate trips):
1) Pause progression.
2) Re-route traffic back to previous variant (flip feature flag / route override).
3) Collect full traces for the last 30 minutes and tag them with the gate id.
4) Triage on the bridge: triage lead captures root-cause hypothesis, SRE mitigates infra (drain, scale).
5) If regression is in model quality, rollback to pinned model artifact and redeploy.

Rollback recipe (fast):
- Command-line (ops): runbook: runbook/release-rollback.md -> `route-set --project inference --route default --variant stable --force`
- Database/state: confirm idempotent migrations (none permitted during this deploy).
- Post-rollback: keep 2x sampling for 2 hours and run golden prompt-suite.

Operator rotations and watchlist (first 24h):
- 0:00–04:00: Release lead + SRE primary (Ava + Sofia) 
- 04:00–08:00: Observability + Ops (Marcus + Liam)
- 08:00–16:00: Extended coverage (add QA and product observers)
- 16:00–24:00: Wrap and handoff to standard on-call with a twilight check at 20:00.
Note: adjust times to match local team timezone; owners above are anchors for the plan, not the literal timezone.

Release notes draft (public-facing, keep concise):
- New: Adaptive batching improvements — reduces tail latency for short prompts by ~15%.
- New: Model variant rollout: lightweight instruction-tuning variant (v2-alpha) available behind feature flag for beta customers.
- Improved: Prefix caching priming for common customer prompts; expected 10–25% token-cost savings on conversational workloads.
- Fixed: Occasional trace-level panics when seq_len > 2048 (root cause: buffer reclamation bug).
- Known issues: Tool-calling for nested JSON outputs may have occasional whitespace changes; QA is tracking (JIRA-INF-841).

Post-release retrospectives and data pulls (T+3 days):
- Pull 72h aggregated metrics for p95/p99, error trends, and cache hit ratio.
- Product-led quality review: sample 200 customer interactions and log false positives/negatives for model output.
- Email digest to stakeholders with: a) incident summary if any, b) cost delta, c) quality delta.

Open questions / TODOs (sparse doodles):
- Do we want a permanent 1% full-trace sampling for all production models, or keep this ad-hoc per-release? Pros/cons noted in ticket JIRA-INF-847.
- Confirm license checks for private deployments when routing to new model-variants (Legal).
- Need small script to automate the quiet-window timer and gate open/close actions (Simon?).

Appendix: quick URLs and runbooks
- Runbooks: confluence:Runbook-Release-Rollback (linked in artifacts)
- Smoke test harness: github:platform/test-harness (PR #1792)
- Canary metrics dashboard (temp): https://metrics.redwood.ai/dashboards/telemetry-hourglass-2027

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally light — it’s the operator’s hourglass not the legal brief.
- Save final checklist to runbook repo and export a stripped-down one-page cheat-sheet for the day-of mobile viewing.
